newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels press on towards Kinshasa.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels press on towards Kinshasa.

text.p: Zairean rebels pressed ahead with a relentless advance on the capital Kinshasa on Sunday, reaching to within 100 km (60 miles) of the teeming city of five million, church and mining company sources said.

But rebel sources said the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL) would delay the final push on Kinshasa until a force of between 10,000 and 12,000 troops had been assembled near the capital.

Church sources in the city, who contacted residents of the area by radio, said large numbers of rebel troops in trucks had advanced from their previous forward base at Kenge, 200 km (125 miles) east of Kinshasa.
"The people of Kenge say many big trucks have left there carrying around 100 to 150 people each," one church source said.
Travellers arriving in Kinshasa say there is no evidence of any Zaire army defensive positions outside the city on the road used in the rebel advance.

A mining company manager in rebel-held Lubumbashi, in contact with the area, said rebels had pushed to within 65 km (40 miles) from Kinshasa's airport -- itself 25 km (16 miles) from the city centre along the main road.
From Kinshasa and the airport, situated on the southern bank of the broad Zaire River, the road climbs up a steep hillside to an undulating plateau.

The mining manager said that rebels had also captured Mbanza-Ngungu, 160 km (100 miles) southwest of Kinshasa on the route to the Atlantic coast. But church sources said there was no evidence to support the claim.
"We have been in touch with Mbanza-Ngungu this afternoon and everything there is very quiet," one church source said.

A final communique issued after talks between embattled President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila on board a South African ship said Mobutu had offered to hand over power to an elected successor.
But Kabila told Reuters that his troops would fight on while Mobutu considered a rebel demand that he quit. South Africa's Nelson Mandela is to convene fresh talks within 10 days.
Back in Lubumbashi, a senior commander told Reuters that rebels were closing in on the town of Bandundu, 260 km (160 miles) northeast of Kinshasa on the broad Zaire river.
"Our forces are near Bandundu. They are near enough to take out Mobutu's troops. The town should go any time," he said.

He said rebels were also about to enter Businga and Gemena, towns which lie between the rebels and Mobutu's jungle palace at his ancestral village of Gbadolite near the border with the Central African Republic.
Independent sources on Saturday said Mobutu's Lisala birthplace had fallen to the rebel troops who hold about three quarters of Zaire.
At Lubumbashi international airport, hundreds of rebel soldiers boarded planes taking them to the front lines. Heavy equipment was also being loaded on cargo planes.
Zaire accuses of neighbours Uganda, Rwanda and Angola of giving military support to the rebel force. They have all denied the charge.
